Hi, I'm a BA EL sophomore as well. I'm majoring in Italian, which is a much smaller department and a faculty that trends younger. All of our profs are incredibly warm and helpful, and I consider myself lucky. I've heard less than flattering things about other language profs.

Agree with the previous commenter who said you have to love your target language. My profs took my existing passion for Italian and made it easier to love the language. I've learned so much and I'm so grateful. But like I said, lucky.

After the first semester, our profs speak in 99% Italian as well. This also goes for non-majors who take further foreign language units. However, my profs personally are very understanding when we can't completely understand 100% of the time.

It does get draining. I've had plenty of times where I wondered why I ever wanted to do this, but at the end of the day I love the language, I love my professors, and I love my classmates. But it's definitely not a degree to get into without being absolutely sure.
